results.status: ✗ BATCH 2 SYSTEMATIC ERROR - 87% error rate (20/23 words)

batch_2_ity_acity_osity_words.critical_finding: Family structure uses VERB STEMS for -ity words, but -ity derives from ADJECTIVES
examples_of_errors: capacity: 'cap + acity' WRONG → should be 'capac + ity' (from adjective capax)
tenacity: 'ten + acity' WRONG → should be 'tenac + ity' (from adjective tenax)
fertility: 'fer + tility' WRONG → should be 'fertil + ity' (from adjective fertilis)
versatility: 'vert + ility' WRONG → should be 'versatil + ity' (from adjective versatilis)
batch_2_ity_acity_osity_words.root_cause: Fundamental misunderstanding in family structure: -tion words derive from verbs (verb stem + -tion = action noun), but -ity words derive from adjectives (adjective stem + -ity = quality noun). Family data conflates these two sources.

verification_progress.scope: 1,161 curated words from all 28 family files

verification_status.batch_2_ity_acity: ✗ SYSTEMATIC ERRORS FOUND (20/23 words need correction)

issue_1.name: Verb stem vs Adjective stem confusion
issue_1.description: Family structure assumes all -ity words are verb derivatives with added suffix, but actually derive from adjective forms
issue_1.impact: All Batch 2 words require morpheme breakdown corrections

issue_2.name: Nominalization stem representation
issue_2.description: Edge cases (fermentation, standardization) may use non-standard derivation paths

issue_3.name: Missing intermediate derivation steps
issue_3.description: Some words (superficiality, specificity) go through noun intermediates before adjective

what_this_means.verification_reveals: Family structure is a good starting point but contains systematic errors in morpheme decomposition, particularly for word classes that derive from different parts of speech (verbs vs adjectives)
what_this_means.user_statement_explanation: This is the 'real and deep problem' the user referenced when saying 'Nothing is verified from family research. It's better than engine but it's still very prone to errors.' The family structure has good word coverage but uses wrong morpheme sources for major word classes.
what_this_means.confidence_level: HIGH - Issues are systematic and reproducible, not random errors
